# implicit-sdf.library: UnsignedDistanceToTriangle

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The unsigned distance from a point to the triangle patch with the given
> vertices. Zero on the patch, positive everywhere else; a degenerate
> (collinear) triangle has a zero normal, which fails the inside test and leaves
> the edge branch — the right answer for a shape that is a segment. Exact.
> (IQ: udTriangle.)

## Signature

```plato
UnsignedDistanceToTriangle(p: Point3D, a: Point3D, b: Point3D, c: Point3D): Number
```

### Law_PlanarTriangleAgreesWithSpatialPatch

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 311](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L311)

```plato
// The planar triangle and the spatial triangle patch describe the same shape
// once the query is coplanar with it: outside they are both the distance to the
// nearest edge, and inside the patch reports zero where the solid reports a
// negative depth. Two independently written bodies with two different inside
// tests, forced to agree.
Law_PlanarTriangleAgreesWithSpatialPatch(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Boolean
    => UnsignedDistanceToTriangle(
            Point3D(p.X, p.Y, 0.0),
            Point3D(a.X, a.Y, 0.0),
            Point3D(b.X, b.Y, 0.0),
            Point3D(c.X, c.Y, 0.0))
        .LawEq(DistanceToTriangle(p, a, b, c).Max(0.0));
```

### Line 959

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato, line 959](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato#L959).

```plato

    //==
    // # Unsigned distance primitives for flat patches in space
    //
    // A triangle or a quadrilateral in space is a ZERO-THICKNESS patch: it has a
    // boundary but no interior, so there is no inside for a sign to report. These
    // bodies return the unsigned distance to the patch — non-negative everywhere and
    // zero exactly on it — and the name says so. Subtract a half-thickness to get a
    // genuine solid: the result is the patch's Minkowski sum with a ball, a rounded
    // plate whose distance is exact.
    //
    // Both work the same way: the three (or four) edge half-plane tests decide
    // whether the query projects INSIDE the patch. When it does, the answer is the
    // perpendicular distance to the patch's plane; when it does not, it is the
    // distance to the nearest edge segment. Under the same portability rules as the
    // rest of the primitive family.

    // The unsigned distance from a point to the triangle patch with the given
    // vertices. Zero on the patch, positive everywhere else; a degenerate
    // (collinear) triangle has a zero normal, which fails the inside test and leaves
    // the edge branch — the right answer for a shape that is a segment. Exact.
    // (IQ: udTriangle.)
    UnsignedDistanceToTriangle(p: Point3D, a: Point3D, b: Point3D, c: Point3D): Number {
        var ba = a.Between(b);
        var cb = b.Between(c);
        var ac = c.Between(a);
        var pa = a.Between(p);
        var pb = b.Between(p);
        var pc = c.Between(p);
        var normal = ba.Cross(ac);
        var insideVotes = ba.Cross(normal).Dot(pa).Sign
                        + cb.Cross(normal).Dot(pb).Sign
                        + ac.Cross(normal).Dot(pc).Sign;
        var toEdges = EdgeOffset(ba, pa).LengthSquared
            .Min(EdgeOffset(cb, pb).LengthSquared)
            .Min(EdgeOffset(ac, pc).LengthSquared);
        var toPlane = normal.Dot(pa) * normal.Dot(pa) / normal.LengthSquared;
        return (insideVotes < 2 ? toEdges : toPlane).Sqrt;
    }
```
